title = "Mother-Daughter Duel (1)"

<p>“That’s enough for today.”</p><p>“Kehk…! Hah…!”</p><p>Seo-eun was crawling on the ground, gasping for breath.</p><p>Today’s personal training had been a notch more intense than yesterday—swordsmanship drills using training blades.</p><p>‘It’s just dodging and light taps, but even this is a decent workout…’</p><p>Now that he thought about it, it had been a while since he’d been in actual combat. In principle, instructors weren’t assigned to Hunter Association missions unless it was a designated task, so opportunities to enter Gates or take on other assignments were rare. That said, as long as they returned on time, clearing low-ranked Gates was tacitly permitted.</p><p>He could see why A-rank Hunters avoided becoming instructors.</p><p>Low pay was one thing, but the lack of Gate runs meant their combat skills inevitably dulled.</p><p>‘Not like I’ll be doing this for long anyway…’</p><p>He took a swig of water while seated on the bench in the personal training area.</p><p>Seo-eun, perhaps cramping up, clutched her thigh and staggered to her feet, trembling as she made her way over.</p><p>“Want some water?”</p><p>“Hah…! Y-yes!”</p><p>As soon as he handed it over, Seo-eun pressed the bottle to her lips without hesitation and started chugging.</p><p>“Haa… I think I can breathe again…”</p><p>She held out the now-empty bottle and plopped down beside him.</p><p>“Then… see you Friday.”</p><p>He stood to leave, but Seo-eun grabbed the hem of his shirt.</p><p>“Can’t we… just sit together a little longer before you go?”</p><p>“…”</p><p>‘Well… if it’s just for a bit.’</p><p>Seo-eun kept stealing glances at him while rubbing her arms and legs. She even massaged her stomach, wincing—probably sore from where he’d struck her during training.</p><p>‘I should go easier on her next time.’</p><p>“Instructor, can I ask you something?”</p><p>“Sure.”</p><p>“Why do you do this?”</p><p>“Hmm?”</p><p>“Other instructors just kill time until their shift ends, but you… you actually teach us properly…”</p><p>Hearing that he was considered diligent made him wonder just how half-assed the previous instructors had been.</p><p>“I’m not going out of my way. This is just the standard training students should receive.”</p><p>“Even the personal training with me?”</p><p>Seo-eun gave him a sly smile. Whether she genuinely wanted an answer or just enjoyed watching him flustered, he had no reason to be flustered or refuse to answer.</p><p><img src="data:image/webp;base64," alt="290835" loading="lazy">
</p><p>“Personal training is… because Seo-eun and I always hide and play it safe in the team. The previous instructor gave high scores for some reason, but I won’t. In fact, I have a question for you too. You’re pretty strong among the trainees, so why don’t you participate more actively in training?”</p><p>“Did you train in the special class, Instructor?”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>Seo-eun was still smiling, but this time, it looked bitter.</p><p>“People like us… we don’t fit in anywhere. To regular people, we’re Awakened, but among Awakened, we’re the weak ones… so we don’t have big dreams.”</p><p>“···.”</p><p>I understood what Seo-eun was trying to say. They had a painfully clear grasp of their place in the world.</p><p>Even after graduation, aside from the rare few who bloomed late, most would end up as C to E-rank Hunters.</p><p>Realistically, very few would even reach C-rank—over 90 percent would likely spend their lives at D or E-rank.</p><p>They had no reason or motivation to get stronger. Their future was simply earning a higher salary than a regular job while clearing E-rank gates for the rest of their lives.</p><p>Their mindset was just to avoid the most undesirable and sometimes despised role in E-rank gates—the “porter.”</p><p>Even when I was in the special class, I considered myself average compared to my peers.</p><p>And yet, I still had the ambition to reach higher and a curiosity about gates.</p><p>But the regular class trainees were being trained in a state where those feelings had been fundamentally neutered.</p><p>‘Was I… too arrogant?’</p><p>Maybe the previous instructors’ lax attitudes had a reason. </p><p>‘Probably the mindset was, “Most of them will just clear E-rank gates their whole lives, so just teach them enough not to die there.”’</p><p>“Still…”</p><p>As I stared at Seo-eun in silence, she spoke up.</p><p>“Still… after personal training, I feel like I’m getting a little stronger. Some of my peers who had no motivation before are starting to want to get stronger too.”</p><p>“Yes, that’s good to hear… Not sure if it’ll motivate you, but clearing D-rank gates pays a lot better than E-rank ones…”</p><p>Seo-eun burst into laughter at my answer, then stood up.</p><p>“There are others who want personal training too… so don’t push them too hard.”</p><p>‘I’ve never pushed anyone hard…’</p><p>“Then I’ll be going!”</p><p>With that, Seo-eun bowed her head in greeting and left the training ground.</p><p>***</p><p>“You’ve gotten a year older…”</p><p>It had already been over three months since I started working as an instructor. Ever since I got a job, my life had settled into a regular, repetitive routine.</p><p>Teach hard, fuck hard…</p><p>Min Se-rin and I had been sleeping together about once every two weeks.</p><p>Since I was a dispatched instructor, I hadn’t expected to stay long, but when I asked if she was planning to quit, she said she’d applied for an extension.</p><p>‘Guess she’s not even trying to hide her true feelings anymore…’</p><p>Still, she looked a lot more energetic than before, so that was a relief.</p><p>The only new thing in my monotonous life was that my new car had finally arrived. Now I could drive anywhere I wanted.</p><p>‘Maybe I should take Ji-hyeon on a family trip in this car before she starts college…’</p><p>I opened the door to bring up the travel idea, only to find Yu-na and Ji-hyeon in the middle of an argument at the table.</p><p>Na-hyeon was sitting on the living room sofa, laughing as she ate fruit, seemingly entertained by their fight.</p><p>“Seong-hyeon, come sit here.”</p><p>I sat down next to Na-hyeon, and she picked up a strawberry and put it in my mouth.</p><p>It was a peaceful Sunday, a rare day when the whole family was home together. I wondered why they were fighting.</p><p>“What are you two… doing?”</p><p>“Well… Ji-hyeon’s starting college soon. I just assumed she’d live in the dorms, but she seems to think she’ll live on her own.”</p><p>“Can’t she just live alone? I could even help her find a place…”</p><p>“Ugh, if you keep solving everything with money, she’ll turn out spoiled. And if Ji-hyeon lives alone, she’ll probably go out drinking every night.”</p><p>“Ji-hyeon?”</p><p>As soon as I said it, I remembered her gap year. Whenever she had free time or her academy was closed, she’d sleep over at friends’ houses like it was nothing.</p><p>And even now, after finishing her retake, she still went out every evening, coming home late or staying out overnight.</p><p>“Yeah, probably…”</p><p>“Mhm.”</p><p>Ji-hyeon had gone through middle school, high school, and even a gap year surrounded only by girls, but once she got to college, she might start drinking with guys.</p><p>“But… I never went to college, so I don’t know, but can’t she just drink with guys? Not every guy who asks her out for drinks has some shady intentions.”</p><p>Na-hyeon listened to me, her eyes widening before she burst into laughter and poked my stomach.</p><p>“After you’ve fucked the whole family, you’re asking if she can’t just drink with guys? Do you really think that?”</p><p>“Watch your mouth…”</p><p>Suddenly, the memory of when Min Se-rin and I had drunkenly made a mistake resurfaced.</p><p>I closed my eyes and silently nodded.</p><p>“Now that I think about it again, it really is dangerous…”</p><p>Alcohol is the root of all evil. That cursed liquid numbs reason, amplifies emotions, and drives people to make mistakes they’d never commit sober.</p><p>And just imagining some other man leering at a drunk Ji-hyeon made murderous rage boil inside me.</p><p>“Right? I told you it was dangerous.”</p><p>As their argument grew more heated, an inexplicable unease washed over me.</p><p>Whenever I got this feeling, the best move was always to leave as quickly as possible.</p><p>Just as I was about to stand up from the sofa and return to my room, Ji-hyeon turned her head toward me and said,</p><p>“Th-then, oppa, you decide! You’re the head of this household, right?”</p><p>“Huh? Me? Why?”</p><p>Caught off guard by the sudden demand, I stammered in confusion. Na-hyeon giggled, as if she found it amusing, and turned her head away.</p><p>I looked at Yu-na in a panic, but she simply gave a slight nod, as if to say, *You decide.*</p><p>“That sounds good. Since you’re my husband, you should decide…”</p><p>At some point, Yu-na had started calling me “yeobo” even when the others were around.</p><p>I was a little surprised at first, but since Na-hyeon and Ji-hyeon didn’t seem to mind, I just went with it.</p><p>‘Only when it’s convenient, huh…’</p><p>Yu-na just wore a triumphant expression, as if the moment she asked me, the battle was already won.</p><p>That confidence could only come from the fact that she was my wife and the mistress of this house.</p><p>I lowered my head and thought.</p><p>Last month, when Ji-hyeon and I went to the department store together, I’d seen a group of men approach her while I was in the restroom. One of them, looking nervous, had shuffled over and tried to get her number by handing her his phone.</p><p>I’d found it amusing, so I didn’t interfere and just watched. And Ji-hyeon had rejected the man with a far more hostile and annoyed expression than when she’d first met me.</p><p>‘She’d probably be fine living alone…’</p><p>Ji-hyeon wasn’t a man-hater, but she was naturally cold toward men she wasn’t close to.</p><p>Even if such a situation arose, she’d likely handle it on her own.</p><p>“S-she’s an adult now, so living alone should be—”</p><p>“Right?”</p><p>“…”</p><p>Yu-na crossed her arms and stared at me in silence, her gaze heavy.</p><p>Instantly, my breath caught in my throat, and the words died on my lips.</p><p>That look in her eyes carried an unspoken pressure, as if to say, *‘How dare you take Ji-hyeon’s side over mine?’*</p><p>“So… even if she’s an adult…”</p><p>“Why are you suddenly changing your tune?”</p><p>“No… that’s not what I meant… I’m just saying…”</p><p>This time, even Ji-hyeon crossed her arms and stared at me.</p><p>“Pfft.”</p><p>Na-hyeon seemed to find the whole situation amusing—she’d sprawled out on the sofa, using the fruit plate like a popcorn bucket, and kept poking my butt with her foot.</p><p>‘I just want to jump out the window right now.’</p><p>There was no escaping this.</p><p>The only way out was to avoid the issue for now and figure out a solution later.</p><p>“L-Look, I need to hear both of your opinions before I can make a decision… You’re both too worked up to think straight right now… I have work tomorrow, and I’ll be back Wednesday morning, so let’s talk then and decide on Thursday.”</p><p>“Fine…”</p><p>“Okay.”</p><p>Fortunately, both women nodded in agreement.</p><p>They each wore smug, confident expressions, as if they’d already won.</p><p>“Phew…”</p><p>“Cheer up.”</p><p>Na-hyeon patted my shoulder a couple times before heading back to her room.</p><p>***</p><p>“What am I supposed to do…”</p><p>I’d barely managed to end the standoff, and we ate dinner. It was the same as usual, but an odd tension lingered in the air, making the meal uncomfortable.</p><p>I’d bought myself two days—Monday and Tuesday—but come Wednesday, I’d have to listen to both of them, and by Thursday, I’d have to make a decision.</p><p>‘I get where my parents are coming from, but Na-hyeon’s an adult now too…’</p><p>“This is complicated… Let’s just get some sleep.”</p><p>I still had two days to think it over, so I could take my time.</p><p>Knock knock.</p><p>Just then, someone knocked on my door.</p><p>“Yeah, come in.”</p><p>No sooner had the words left my mouth than the door swung open, revealing Ji-hyeon in a sleepwear so sheer it made my face burn.</p><p>“W-What…”</p><p>Ji-hyeon swayed over to the window, gripping the curtains as she spoke.</p><p><img src="data:image/webp;base64," alt="290836" loading="lazy">
</p><p>“Oh, nothing… I just wanted to see oppa before bed.”</p><p>It seemed their battle had already begun.</p>
